language.name: Java
language.justification: Provides long-term support, high performance, and strong typing suitable for complex business logic.

framework.name: Spring Boot
framework.justification: Matches the preferred stack constraint and offers mature modular enterprise capabilities.

database.name: PostgreSQL
database.justification: Delivers ACID compliance, native JSON support, and robust Row-Level Security for future multi-tenancy.

cache.name: Redis
cache.justification: Handles user sessions, distributed rate limiting, and frequently read catalog caches efficiently.

message_broker.name: None
message_broker.justification: An external message broker is omitted to avoid unnecessary operational overhead for 200 concurrent users.

authentication_mechanism.name: Spring Security with JWT
authentication_mechanism.justification: Provides stateless bearer token authentication compatible with web clients and future multi-tenant SaaS needs.

frontend.name: React
frontend.justification: Provides a robust component ecosystem suitable for complex ERP data grids on desktop and tablet browsers.

multi_tenancy.details: All tenant-scoped tables include a mandatory tenant_id column enforced via Hibernate filters and PostgreSQL Row-Level Security.

authentication_and_authorization.rbac_enforcement: Controller and service layers via Spring Security method annotations evaluated against claims in the token.

error_format_and_status_codes.status_code_conventions: Standard HTTP semantics (400 Bad Request, 401 Unauthorized, 403 Forbidden, 404 Not Found, 409 Conflict, 422 Unprocessable Entity, 500 Internal Error).

logging_audit_and_observability.logging: Structured JSON logging via Logback with correlation IDs propagated through MDC.
logging_audit_and_observability.audit: Synchronous recording of critical mutations and sensitive data access to a dedicated audit store.
logging_audit_and_observability.observability: Micrometer exporting Prometheus metrics and OpenTelemetry traces.

configuration_and_secrets.strategy: Environment variables managed externally via AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store and AWS Secrets Manager.

data_conventions.timestamps_and_timezone: UTC stored as TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE and serialized as ISO 8601 strings.
data_conventions.soft_delete: Supported via deleted_at timestamp column on transactional records; excluded from unique constraints.
data_conventions.money_and_decimals: DECIMAL(19, 4) for monetary amounts and quantities to eliminate floating-point rounding errors.

api_conventions.pagination: Keyset pagination for unbounded queries and offset-limit for bounded UI data tables.

direct_call.when_to_use: Synchronous query and read-only lookups across module boundary interfaces within the same transaction.

events.when_to_use: Decoupled state change notifications using Spring Application Events for non-blocking secondary workflows.
events.delivery_guarantee: At-least-once via transactional event listener with persistent outbox fallback

queue.when_to_use: Not utilized within the modular monolith deployment footprint.

module_map.name: Users
module_map.responsibility: Manages user accounts, authentication tokens, password lifecycles, and role-based permissions.

module_map.name: Audit
module_map.responsibility: Captures and exposes an immutable centralized log of business actions and user activity.

module_map.name: Customers
module_map.responsibility: Maintains registries for customers and suppliers including contacts, addresses, and credit limits.

module_map.name: Catalog
module_map.responsibility: Maintains product registries, categories, units of measure, and active price lists.

module_map.name: Inventory
module_map.responsibility: Tracks physical stock balances per warehouse, stock transfers, and manual inventory adjustments.

module_map.name: Purchasing
module_map.responsibility: Manages purchase requisitions, supplier quotes, purchase orders, and goods receipt.

module_map.name: Sales
module_map.responsibility: Handles sales quotes, order validation, credit checks, inventory reservation requests, and fulfillment dispatch.

module_map.name: Finance
module_map.responsibility: Controls accounts payable, accounts receivable, payment settlements, and monthly accounting closes.

decisions.context: Selecting the foundational architecture for an ERP serving 200 peak concurrent users with limited team operational bandwidth.
decisions.decision: Modular monolith with strictly defined package boundaries and in-memory module interfaces.
decisions.consequences: Drastically reduces infrastructure complexity while retaining clear boundaries that enable a future microservices split if required.

decisions.context: Architecting multi-tenancy for a system starting as single-company but targeting future SaaS commercialization.
options_considered: Shared database with tenant discriminator column
decisions.decision: Shared database using a tenant_id discriminator column enforced via Row-Level Security.
decisions.consequences: Minimizes initial infrastructure costs and maintenance complexity while enforcing strict logical separation across queries.

decisions.context: Selecting primary key representation for high-write ERP entities that require security and sortability.
decisions.decision: Adopt UUIDv7 as the universal primary key type.
decisions.consequences: Prevents enumeration attacks across tenants while maintaining B-tree index locality and insertion performance.

decisions.context: Managing decoupled inter-module notifications without introducing heavy broker infrastructure.
options_considered: Spring Application Events with PostgreSQL Transactional Outbox
decisions.decision: Use Spring in-memory Application Events backed by a PostgreSQL Transactional Outbox for critical side effects.
decisions.consequences: Ensures transactionally safe event handling without managing an external message broker cluster.

decisions.context: Balancing LGPD right-to-erasure requirements with statutory 5-year financial record retention.
options_considered: PII anonymization with immutable financial snapshot retention
decisions.decision: Anonymize personal information in customer registries while preserving immutable financial transaction records.
decisions.consequences: Satisfies both Brazilian data privacy compliance and mandatory tax audit retention standards.

risks.risk: Accidental data leakage across tenants if tenant discriminator filters are omitted in custom queries.
risks.mitigation: Enforce PostgreSQL Row-Level Security policies at the database engine level in addition to application-level ORM filters.

risks.risk: Performance degradation during month-end financial closing peaks due to contested stock and ledger rows.
risks.mitigation: Use read replicas for financial reporting and apply pessimistic locking with short timeouts strictly to active close transactions.

risks.risk: Monolith package boundary erosion through direct entity sharing across module boundaries.
risks.mitigation: Enforce architectural boundaries and package-private access rules at build time using ArchUnit.

assumptions.decision: The web frontend will be developed as a responsive Single Page Application using React and TypeScript.
assumptions.reason: The constraints specify desktop and tablet browser usage without specifying a frontend technology.

assumptions.decision: The system will initially be deployed with a single default tenant identifier hardcoded in application configuration.
assumptions.reason: Allows single-company deployment today while satisfying the constraint of future multi-tenant SaaS readiness.

assumptions.decision: No external message broker will be provisioned in the initial AWS infrastructure environment.
assumptions.reason: An expected load of 200 concurrent users does not warrant the cost and complexity of a separate broker.

assumptions.decision: Direct inter-warehouse stock movements are assumed to be immediate without intermediate in-transit shipping states for the MVP.
assumptions.reason: The inventory module specification lists warehouse transfers without defining complex in-transit logistics.
